We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

Let's parse: It's a tolyl (para methyl phenyl) attached to sulfonamide linking to another phenyl ring bearing a trans-α,β-unsaturated amide attached to an aniline (Nc3ccccc3N). Actually the amide is C(=O)N attached to an aniline (anilide) with an extra NH on the aniline? Wait: C(=O)N c3ccccc3N means the amide nitrogen attached to phenyl which also has an NH substituent (aniline). So overall three fragments: a tolyl sulfonyl chloride derived sulfonamide, a phenyl ring with a trans-alkene and amide, and an aniline.

The guidance: three steps: 1) sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). 2) Doebner modification to form α,β-unsaturated acid from aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid then decarboxylation? Actually Doebner modification yields α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid from aldehyde. Then 3) amide coupling of that acid with aniline.

Thus retrosynthesis: target -> disconnect amide bond between C(=O) and N of aniline -> gives α,β-unsaturated acid fragment: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/CO)cc2)cc1? Wait the acid would be the unsaturated acid: the fragment /C=C/C(=O)OH attached to phenyl-sulfonamide. So precursor 1: α,β-unsaturated acid (trans) attached to phenyl-sulfonamide. Precursor 2: aniline (c3ccccc3N). Then step 2: disconnect the C=C double bond formation via Doebner: the unsaturated acid derived from aromatic aldehyde (the phenyl-sulfonamide bearing aldehyde) + malonic acid -> gives unsaturated acid after decarboxylation. So precursor: aromatic aldehyde (phenyl-sulfonamide with aldehyde at para position). That aldehyde is attached to phenyl-sulfonamide: c2ccc(CHO)cc2 attached to sulfonamide. So we need that aldehyde.

Step 3: sulfonamide formation: the phenyl-sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CH3?) Actually the sulfonyl chloride is p-tolylsulfonyl chloride? Wait the sulfonamide is NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(... ) . The sulfonyl group attached to the tolyl amine? The sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to tolyl ring (the first phenyl with methyl). So the sulfonyl chloride would be p-toluenesulfonyl chloride (TsCl) reacting with the aniline of the second phenyl? Actually the sulfonamide nitrogen is attached to the tolyl ring (the first phenyl). So the sulfonyl chloride is attached to the second phenyl? Let's examine: Cc1ccc(N S(=O)(=O) c2ccc(... ) cc2) cc1. So the sulfonyl group is attached to the tolyl amine (the nitrogen attached to tolyl). So the sulfonyl chloride would be the sulfonyl part attached to the second phenyl (c2ccc...). So we need sulfonyl chloride: ClSO2-Ph-... where the phenyl has the unsaturated acid substituent (later). So step 3: sulfonamide formation between tolyl amine (p-toluidine) and sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride bearing aldehyde). So precursors: p-toluidine (4-methylaniline) and aryl sulfonyl chloride (ClSO2-Ph-CHO). The sulfonyl chloride can be derived from the corresponding sulfonic acid (by chlorination) but we can treat as available.

Thus route: 1) amide coupling: unsaturated acid + aniline -> target. 2) Doebner: aldehyde + malonic acid -> unsaturated acid. 3) sulfonamide formation: p-toluidine + aryl sulfonyl chloride (aryl sulfonyl chloride derived from same aldehyde? Actually the aldehyde is on the sulfonyl chloride phenyl, so the sulfonyl chloride already contains the aldehyde. So step 3 uses that sulfonyl chloride and p-toluidine.

Thus we need to propose template IDs for each step. We need to search for templates matching these transformations.

First step: amide formation from carboxylic acid and amine (functional_groups_broken: aliphatic carboxylic acid, functional_groups_formed: amide). We attempted search but got empty. Maybe need to specify "carboxylic esters" broken? Actually coupling breaks carboxylic acid (C-O) and forms amide (C-N). The functional group broken is "aliphatic carboxylic acid". That is valid. But no templates found maybe due to limited catalog. Could try "carboxylic esters" broken? But we need acid. Let's try search with bonds broken/formed. Use bonds broken: "C-O" and bonds formed: "C-N".
